provenance.note: Generated once from an independent reference implementation and checked in. The hashes identify exactly which inputs produced these numbers; regenerating against the same inputs reproduces the file byte for byte.

cases.name: gaussian_shared
cases.why: the gaussian kernel on one shared radius, which is the case where matrix() is symmetric and the transpose in solve() cannot be caught (the reference implementation:888-891)

cases.name: linear_shared
cases.why: the linear kernel on the same poses: compact support, so it reaches exactly zero at the radius and the weights fall to nothing outside

cases.name: gaussian_per_pose
cases.why: per-pose radii, which make matrix() asymmetric and are the only configuration that tells the transposed inverse from the untransposed one (the reference implementation:881-900)

cases.name: linear_per_pose
cases.why: the same asymmetry under the compact kernel

cases.name: pose_type_whole
cases.why: poseType 0: every pose measured on the whole rotation

cases.name: pose_type_swing
cases.why: poseType 1 (the reference implementation:479-483): the swing half only, so a pure twist leaks nothing into a bend pose

cases.name: pose_type_mixed
cases.why: one interpolator carrying all three, which is what the data actually authors and what makes distance() belong to the POSE rather than to the interpolator

cases.name: twist_axis_x
cases.why: the twist axis is the driver's, not always Y: driverTwistAxis 0 (the reference implementation)

cases.name: translation_only
cases.why: enableRotation off: a face driver whose rotations are noise and whose poses are millimetres apart. Measured as a rotation it is degenerate (the reference implementation:804-837); measured on the channel that drives it, it separates cleanly

cases.name: translation_only_linear
cases.why: the same, under the compact kernel

cases.name: both_channels
cases.why: enableRotation AND enableTranslation: radians against metres, combined as a right-angled triangle after each is divided by its own falloff (the reference implementation:149-214)

cases.name: normalize_off
cases.why: normalize off: the raw solve, so the normalisation step can be told apart from the multiply it follows

cases.name: normalize_refused
cases.why: a narrow linear kernel, so most random samples land where every kernel is zero and |sum| < 1e-6. the reference implementation:985 leaves the weights alone there rather than dividing by almost nothing

cases.name: clamp_negative
cases.why: allowNegativeWeights off: the clamp is max(0, w) applied AFTER normalisation (the reference implementation), never before and never inside the solve

cases.name: clamp_negative_per_pose
cases.why: the same clamp where the negatives are large, because per-pose widths are what produce them

cases.name: regularized
cases.why: regularization on coincident poses: a nudge on the diagonal that separates them, so _invert never raises

cases.name: singular
cases.why: two poses exactly on top of each other with no regularization: _invert raises, solve() nudges the diagonal by SINGULAR = 1e-12 and inverts again (the reference implementation:908-919). The inverse is then ~1e12 and no absolute tolerance is meaningful on it, so only the EVALUATED weights are compared -- they come out at 1/n, which is the flat answer that branch is supposed to give
